script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. September 4th, 2026. Can you believe it's already September?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。2026年9月4日。もう9月って信じられます？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Morning, Alex. Time flies, doesn't it? And it's really coming down out there.
script.ja: おはよう、アレックス。あっという間だね。外はすごい雨だね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, 100% chance of rain today, they said. High of 25.8, low of 20.4. I'm glad I didn't cycle in today.
script.ja: うん、今日は降水確率100%だって。最高25.8度、最低20.4度。今日は自転車で来なくてよかったよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good call. I saw a few people looking pretty soaked on the way in.
script.ja: 正解だね。通勤途中に何人かびしょ濡れの人を見たよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, my morning coffee. That's what I need. I couldn't even finish it at home, the baby was so energetic this morning.
script.ja: あー、朝のコーヒー。これが必要なんだ。家で飲みきれなかったよ、今朝は赤ちゃんがすごく元気でさ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Mine's tea. It's calming.
script.ja: 私は紅茶。落ち着くからね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Calming sounds good. Anyway, welcome back to The Daily Tanu-chan Show! Let's check the news. NHK World had something about Kabuki.
script.ja: 落ち着くのはいいね。さて、ザ・デイリー・たぬちゃん・ショーへようこそ！ニュースをチェックしましょう。NHKワールドで歌舞伎の話題があったね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, 'Roppongi Kabuki Part II Zatoichi.' They said it's the most accessible Kabuki ever. Shorter, easier to understand.
script.ja: ええ、「六本木歌舞伎II ざとういち」。史上最も親しみやすい歌舞伎だそうよ。短くて、分かりやすいって。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I didn't know that. I've always wanted to go, but four hours, not really knowing what's happening... that's a tough sell.
script.ja: へえ、知らなかった。ずっと行ってみたかったんだけど、4時間も何が起こってるか分からないのは…ちょっと大変だよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It can be. My daughter actually saw it with some friends. She said it was interesting.
script.ja: そうね。うちの娘が友達と観に行ったわ。面白かったって言ってた。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Interesting. Maybe I should look into it. With the baby, though, finding time for anything like that is... difficult.
script.ja: 面白いね。調べてみようかな。でも赤ちゃんがいると、そういう時間を見つけるのは…難しいんだよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It gets easier.
script.ja: そのうち楽になるわよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: I hope so. There was also some pretty grim news. An 87-year-old man died in Tottori, pinned by an agricultural transporter.
script.ja: だといいんだけど。あと、ちょっと暗いニュースもあったね。鳥取で87歳の男性が農業用運搬機に挟まれて亡くなったって。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, I saw that. Very sad.
script.ja: ええ、見たわ。とても悲しいことだね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: And an Indonesian trainee died in a mixer at a Hiroshima plant. It's just... awful to hear about work accidents like that.
script.ja: それから、広島の工場でインドネシア人の研修生がミキサーに巻き込まれて亡くなったって。こういう労働災害を聞くのは…本当に辛いね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. Safety should always be the priority.
script.ja: そうだね。安全は常に最優先されるべきだわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Definitely. I mean, if I felt like my workplace wasn't safe, I'd feel pretty... what's the word... `disgruntled`? Is that right?
script.ja: 本当に。もし職場の安全が確保されていないと感じたら、かなり…なんて言うんだっけ…「disgruntled」？それで合ってる？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, `disgruntled` means feeling annoyed or unhappy, especially because something unfair happened.
script.ja: ええ、disgruntledは、特に不公平なことが起こったせいで、不満を感じたり不機嫌になったりすることね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Ah, okay. So, not just generally annoyed, but specifically unhappy about something unfair. Got it. I think a lot of people might be feeling `disgruntled` about this rain, actually.
script.ja: ああ、なるほど。ただイライラしてるんじゃなくて、不公平なことに対して不満を感じている、と。分かった。この雨で不満を感じてる人も多いかもしれないね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Possibly. Especially if it's affecting their commute.
script.ja: そうね。特に通勤に影響が出ている場合はね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Speaking of today, did you know today is Clean Coal Day? Ku (9) Riin (4) Kooru (clean coal). September 4th.
script.ja: ところで今日なんだけど、今日は「クリーン・コール・デー」なんだって知ってた？ク(9)リーン・コ(4)ール。9月4日。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I did. It's to raise awareness about coal as an energy source, especially for its cleaner uses.
script.ja: 知ってたわ。エネルギー源としての石炭、特にクリーンな利用法について認識を高めるための日よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right, I feel like I read about this every year. It's still a big deal for energy, even with all the talk about renewables.
script.ja: ああ、毎年これについて読んでる気がする。再生可能エネルギーの話が多い中でも、石炭はまだエネルギーとして重要なんだよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. It's a complex issue.
script.ja: そうね。複雑な問題だわ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It really is. You know, with this weather, I was thinking about my weekend ride. My bike's going to be `sorely` missed if this rain continues.
script.ja: 本当にそうだね。この天気だと、週末のサイクリングのことを考えちゃうよ。この雨が続くと、自転車が「sorely」寂しくなるな。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: `Sorely` means intensely or very much. So, you'll miss it very much.
script.ja: 「Sorely」は、非常にとか、とてもという意味ね。だから、とても寂しくなる、ということよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Exactly! I'll miss it `sorely`. It's my only escape sometimes, especially now that the baby's crawling everywhere. It's a full-time job chasing after him.
script.ja: そうそう！「sorely」寂しくなるよ。たまに唯一の息抜きなんだ、特に赤ちゃんがどこでもハイハイするようになってから。彼を追いかけるのはフルタイムの仕事だよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I remember those days. My son was very fast.
script.ja: そういう日々を覚えてるわ。うちの息子もとても速かった。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I jump at everything these days. Pretty sure it's the baby. Like, any little noise, I'm just instantly alert. It's exhausting.
script.ja: うん、最近は何にでも飛び起きちゃうよ。きっと赤ちゃんのせいだ。ちょっとした物音でも、すぐに警戒態勢に入るんだ。疲れるよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. That's part of it.
script.ja: そうね。それも一部だよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right. Well, I guess we should probably get to it. Another busy day.
script.ja: だよね。さて、そろそろ仕事に取り掛からないとね。また忙しい一日だ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Have a good one, Alex.
script.ja: 良い一日を、アレックス。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: You too, Sarah. And try to stay dry!
script.ja: サラさんもね。そして、濡れないようにね！

wikipedia.description: 1992（平成4）年、「ク（9）リーン・コ（5）ール」の語呂合わせから、石炭関連団体で構成するクリーン・コール・デー実行委員会が制定。エネルギー源としての石炭を広く認識してもらうため。
